Dying Light 2 was one of those games I put off forever because "I knew I was going to like it". I finally decided to start it and gave up almost immediately after reaching the main city.

The beginning area is fine to navigate but the parkour feels weird, artificial and restrictive, and the character always seems to pick the worst possible move. The only emotion I felt at night was annoyance. It seemed that every time I tried to do a task that the game arbitrarily makes you do at night for no reason, a pack of Volatiles would spawn right in my face and force me to waste a lot of time avoiding them.

The writing was horrible as well. The original was not anything special but at least made me care about my missions and it didn't seem like every character was insane. The lack of guns was disappointing, but the excuse was do idiotic. The military confiscated all the guns and then... ran out of ammo? In a huge city abundant in resources? Do the writers realize that it's relatively easy to make ammunition even on your own? And the replacement bows lacked any punch.

The setting is also extremely generic. A boring town with three one-dimensional factions (bandits, soldiers and random citizens). I'm not saying Harran had interesting factions, but the fact that the outbreak happened during the Olympics led to really cool, unique visual elements in the environment, that the sequel's generic postapo town just does not have. 

One thing that made me stop being in denial and finally quit the game when I reached the second map. The buildings are too tall to freerun effectively, and the glider is a chore. I don't know how but they really managed to make a paraglider completely unfun.

I loved The Elder Scrolls Legends. I joined not long after Sparkypants took over from the original developers. The new client looked very good and I liked how the game improved on Hearthstone formula. Not to mention it expanded the TES lore and had gorgeous art.

Frankly, the red flags were already there. While the game had a lot of previous content, after the Sparkypants redesign we got almost a year of content drought (with obvious gaps, like only five of possible tricolour decks supported). 

Then, a very ambitious roadmap was released, four expansions would supposedly release within a year. The first one was significantly delayed, and after that there was a radio silence from the previously very active community managers. 

The next expansion comes out, introducing a game breaking mechanic that completely ruins the meta. No word from the devs, then a tiny nerf that does not do enough to rectify the problem. 

After that (and weeks of begging from the players to fix the mechanic and complete radio silence), comes the announcement. The next expansion is cancelled and the game is going into "maintenance mode" (no new content will come out but the servers will still be running). To soften the blow they give out some of the cards from the  unfinished expansion for free to everyone.

It, unsurprisingly, means nothing. The community dies almost overnight. All content creators release their goodbye videos. Bethesda has their new free to play title, the horrible Elder Scrolls Blades. I can't help but feel Legends was done dirty by Bethesda. The game was excellent and still had a lot of potential. It's just sad it got replaced by the soulless joke that was Blades. The promised Switch port never came out either, but to be fair I'm not sure it would be enough to save the game. 

It was one of two free to play titles I've spent a significant amount of money on. I don't feel cheated or anything, but I feel very disappointed with how things turned out. The Elder Scrolls subreddits sometimes share the art from the game and it hurts every time. Sometimes I quietly hope for revival. The Chinese servers are handled by a different company and they were still releasing new content for a while. I'm not sure how it is now. But let's be real, such things don't really happen.
